item.title: US woman returns from abroad to find inherited house sold using forged documents
item.description: A Tennessee woman returned from abroad in 2021 to discover that her late brother's house had been sold using a fake identity and forged documents. After she sued the company involved in the sale, a lower court dismissed her case. On Thursday, an appeals court revived her fraud claim but upheld the dismissal of her negligence claim.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Serena Williams helped build 2 schools in rural Kenya; years later, both remain open and part of national education system
item.description: Serena Williams established two secondary schools in rural Kenya to provide local children with education. The Matooni Serena Williams Secondary School opened in 2009, followed by the Wee Serena Williams Secondary School in 2010. Both schools are now integrated into Kenya's national education system and managed by community boards. HP's involvement brought important technology resources to enhance learning experiences for students.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: A Dutch engineer built a car controlled by a goldfish swimming inside a water tank; earning a Guinness World Records title
item.description: In an extraordinary showcase of technology and pet companionship, Blub, the goldfish belonging to Dutch engineer Thomas de Wolf, successfully maneuvered a motion-sensing vehicle for 12.28 meters on a Milan television show aired on January 23, 2025. By translating Blub's natural movements into steering commands, De Wolf envisions applications of this technology to assist people with physical disabilities, merging creativity with functionality.

item.title: California teen wins $10,000 for system that controls computers using tongue movements and blinks
item.description: Hollie Tang, a talented student from Wilson High School, has innovatively developed a system named Tonguage, designed to empower individuals with disabilities. This groundbreaking technology enables users to navigate devices through tongue movements and eye blinks. Winning the top scholarship at the Regeneron International Science and Engineering Fair in Phoenix, Tang highlighted the potential of technology to enhance lives.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Oprah Winfrey’s $60 million Maui wildfire relief fund helped thousands; now her donation brings new CT scanner to local hospital
item.description: Oprah Winfrey and Dwayne Johnson launched the People's Fund of Maui to support wildfire survivors and provided significant financial assistance. Winfrey made a separate donation for a new CT scanner at Maui Memorial Medical Center to enhance healthcare services. The scanner aims to improve diagnosis and treatment for all patients, benefiting the wider Maui community. This contribution is part of a broader effort to strengthen healthcare infrastructure on the island.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Black Hole Blast Shapes Structure: Astronomers trace ‘Treble Clef’ origins; collision revives radio glow
item.description: Astronomers have uncovered that the peculiar Treble Clef formation stems from a black hole eruption and the merger of two galaxy clusters. Observations from a variety of telescopes across different wavelengths revealed that the explosive event launched particles, which were later re-energized through the cluster collision. This groundbreaking research enhances our understanding of how cosmic phenomena can fundamentally alter the structures within the universe.
item.dc:creator: TOI Science Desk

item.title: Teen-Led Wildlife Effort: Georgia student turns Johns Creek into habitat model; certification endures
item.description: In a remarkable effort, Malcolm Barnard led a campaign to promote wildlife conservation in Johns Creek, Georgia, achieving the status of a certified habitat community. He focused on educating the community while engaging schools and organizations to adopt wildlife-friendly practices. By 2013, all public schools in the area were recognized by the National Wildlife Federation, fostering a vision of interconnected habitats rather than isolated green spaces.

item.title: US man marries dying partner in hospital, court reverses ruling voiding marriage
item.description: A Kentucky man who married his partner of nearly 30 years in hospital just 15 days before her death has won an appeal after her daughter challenged the marriage. The daughter questioned her mother's ability to consent and how the marriage licence was obtained. On Friday, the Kentucky Court of Appeals overturned the ruling invalidating the marriage and ordered further examination of the case.
item.dc:creator: TOI World Desk

item.title: Netanyahu pushing Trump for nuclear strike on Iran? US commentator makes big claim
item.description: Tucker Carlson has claimed that Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu is pressuring US President Donald Trump for military action. This action is reportedly a nuclear strike aimed at Pickaxe Mountain in Iran, where nuclear activities are believed to be ongoing. Carlson suggests that the pressure could lead to a decision within days, escalating regional tensions. Diplomatic efforts between the US and Iran continue, though military options remain under consideration.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: Brooklyn woman attacked, stabbed in neck while jogging on waterfront trail
item.description: A 28-year-old woman named Katie Suarez was critically injured during a stabbing incident while jogging. The attack occurred along the Shore Parkway Greenway at around 8 pm local time on October 30. Emergency medical personnel transported Suarez to NYU Langone Hospital-Brooklyn, where she was admitted in critical condition. Police are appealing for information from witnesses to help identify the attacker responsible for the incident.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: US explores route to bring Russian gas back to Europe through Ukraine: Report
item.description: The US is exploring a plan to resume Russian natural gas supplies to Europe through Ukraine as part of efforts to secure an energy ceasefire and advance peace talks. The proposal could offer Moscow a financial incentive while providing Kyiv with transit revenue, but faces strong European opposition amid concerns over renewed dependence on Russia.
item.dc:creator: Abhishek Mishra

item.title: Chinese Airlines Face Losses: Jet fuel surge, weak fares hit Q3 margins; stocks sink this year
item.description: China's leading airlines are experiencing significant financial losses amid rising jet fuel prices and weak domestic fare competition. Air China and China Eastern are expected to report their seventh consecutive annual net loss since the pandemic began. China Southern, after a brief return to profitability, is also projected to return to losses. Analysts indicate that the fourth quarter may continue to be challenging due to high operational expenses.
item.dc:creator: Mahima Sharma

item.title: Fresh Iran strikes after US midterms? Inside Trump-Netanyahu's 'tough' call
item.description: Donald Trump and Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu held a tough phone call regarding Iran and military strategies. They discussed the possibility of military action after the upcoming US midterm elections. Trump expressed readiness for diplomacy, while Netanyahu urged immediate strikes against Iran. Diplomatic initiatives continue, with the US Vice President sending a letter to Iran's national security chief.
item.dc:creator: Yashasvi Vasistha

item.title: £5 ivory chess piece found in family drawer sells for £735,000 after 55 years
item.description: An extraordinary Lewis chessman carving has fetched an impressive £735,000 at auction. Hidden away in a drawer for more than 55 years by the family of the dealer, this remarkable figure was revealed as a warder, part of the legendary Lewis Chessmen collection. Originally found in 1831, this collection comprises 93 intricately carved pieces from 1150 to 1200 AD, though the auction leaves four original pieces still unaccounted for.
